hints: Only the horizontal component of the tension force does work along the horizontal displacement: $F_x = T\cos\theta = 20\cos\theta$.
Calculate the horizontal displacement $s$ of the block moving at constant speed: $s = v \times t = 1.5 \times 12 = 18\text{ m}$.
Use the work done formula $W = F_x \times s = 20\cos\theta \times 18 = 360\cos\theta$.
Set the work done equal to $50\text{ J}$, solve for $\cos\theta = \frac{50}{360}$, and find $\theta = \arccos(5/36)$ to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
State the foundational formula for work done by a constant force inclined at an angle $\theta$ to the direction of motion:
$$W = (T\cos\theta) \times s$$

Find the displacement $s$ of the block using the constant speed formula $\text{distance} = \text{speed} \times \text{time}$:
$$s = 1.5 \times 12 = 18\text{ m}$$

Substitute the tension $T = 20\text{ N}$, displacement $s = 18\text{ m}$, and work done $W = 50\text{ J}$ into the work equation:
$$50 = 20\cos\theta \times 18$$

Multiply the numerical constants on the right side:
$$20 \times 18 = 360 \implies 50 = 360\cos\theta$$

Divide both sides by $360$ to isolate $\cos\theta$:
$$\cos\theta = \frac{50}{360} = \frac{5}{36} \approx 0.138889$$

Take the inverse cosine (arccosine) to determine the angle $\theta$ in degrees:
$$\theta = \arccos(0.138889) \approx 82.019^\circ = 82.0^\circ \text{ (to 3 s.f.)}$$
